words: A trait that helps a plant or animal survive where it lives.
A feature of a living thing, like leaf shape, root depth, or stem thickness.
Something that helps a plant survive or reproduce better than other plants nearby.

parts.title: Traits Help Plants Survive
parts.html:
Every plant has traits: features like leaf shape, root depth, or stem thickness. Some traits help a plant get water. Others help it catch sunlight, stay safe, or make seeds.

When a trait helps a plant survive in its environment, scientists call it an adaptation. A plant with a useful adaptation has an advantage over other plants.

parts.title: Desert Plants vs. Rainforest Plants
parts.html:
Desert plants live with very little water. A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem. Its spines are really leaves with a new shape. They lose almost no water, and they keep animals away.

In a rainforest, rain falls almost every day. Many leaves are wide, to catch light in the shade. Some end in a pointed drip tip. Scientists think drip tips help leaves dry fast, so moss and mold don't grow on them. A trait that helps in one place may hurt in another.

parts.title: Root Systems and Reproduction
parts.html:
The root system is an adaptation too. Desert cactuses have shallow roots that spread wide to catch rain fast. Many grassland plants have deep roots that live through dry weather and fire. Wetland plants have spongy roots that can grow in flooded soil.

Plants also need to reproduce. A plant that lives long enough to make seeds passes its helpful traits on. Over time, the plants with the best traits for a place are the ones that keep growing there.

curator.A: Wide and thin → loses water fast. A wide leaf catches lots of light, which helps in a shady rainforest. In a hot desert, a leaf like this would dry out.
curator.B: Thick and plump → keeps its water. A cactus pad is really a stem. It stores water inside a waxy skin, and its leaves are tiny spines that lose almost none.

mix.q: The prickly pear (Stop 1) and the red mangrove (Stop 4) both grow in Florida. Could they trade places and still do well?

options.t: Yes. They both grow in Florida, so they can grow anywhere in Florida.
options.miss: Same state, but very different places. A cactus in salty, flooded mud could rot. A mangrove on dry sand would dry out.

options.t: No. Each one has traits that fit its own soil and water. In the other place, those traits wouldn't help.
options.ok: Yes! One state can hold very different environments. A trait that helps in dry sand can hurt in salty mud.

wow.title: The fern that comes back to life
wow.alt: Brown, curled-up fern leaves on a tree branch
wow.caption: Resurrection fern, dried and curled up · Cumberland Island, Georgia
wow.html:
This fern grows on the branches of live oak trees all over Florida. In a dry spell, it curls up and turns brown. It looks dead!

Scientists say it can lose almost all of its water and still live. After a good rain, it can turn green again in about a day. It even flew into space on the space shuttle in 1997.
wow.insetCap: The same kind of fern after rain: green and open.

keyIdea: Plants have traits that help them survive in their environment. A trait that gives a plant an advantage is called an adaptation, and a trait that helps in one place may not help at all in another.

quiz.q: What does an adaptation do for a plant?

options.t: It helps the plant grow faster than all other plants.
options.miss: Growing fast isn't the point. An adaptation is about surviving in a certain place. Which choice says that?

options.t: It helps the plant survive in its environment.
options.ok: 🌿 That's it! An adaptation is a trait that helps a plant survive where it lives.

options.t: It makes the plant change color every day.
options.miss: Plants don't change color every day. An adaptation helps a plant survive where it lives. Which choice says that?

quiz.q: A cactus has spines instead of wide leaves. Why is this an advantage in a desert?

options.t: Spines are much smaller than leaves, so the cactus loses less water.
options.ok: 🌵 Exactly right! Wide leaves lose water into the air. Tiny spines lose almost none, a huge advantage when rain is rare.

options.t: Spines catch more sunlight than wide leaves would.
options.miss: Think about what a desert plant needs most. What does a cactus have to hold on to carefully?

options.t: Spines help the cactus absorb more rain during storms.
options.miss: The roots soak up the rain, not the spines. What does a cactus have to hold on to carefully?

quiz.q: A plant has spongy roots that can grow in flooded soil. Where would this trait give it the biggest advantage?

options.t: A desert, where the soil stays dry for months at a time.
options.miss: Think about which place has water in the soil most of the time.

options.t: A grassland, where rain is seasonal and soil drains well.
options.miss: Soil that drains well doesn't stay flooded. Which place has water in the soil most of the time?

options.t: A wetland, where the soil is often waterlogged (soaked).
options.ok: ⭐ Well done! Spongy roots are an adaptation to flooded soil. Most plants would drown there, but wetland plants do well because of that trait.
